performance.verdict: Campaigns dark 2 days; CPL collapse is a delivery gap, not efficiency.

findings.text: Meta went dark Oct 6–7 ($0 spend, 0 leads both days); zero_spend_day flag confirmed. Last 3 days avg spend $11.65 vs prior 3-day avg $43.50 — delivery collapsed.
Pre-launch stack test, Como→GHL migration, GBP triage, Meta account & CAPI, and landing pages — all overdue since 2026-07-31, now 69+ days late. Attribution is blind.
Meta reactivation & persona lanes, Search campaigns, LSA verification, and nurture sequences overdue since 2026-08-31/09-01. Phase 1 close milestone (Sep 30) also missed.
CPL hit $6.25 on 28d blended (+110% week-over-week) but cause is spend concentration: MDST-WES-AWARE-WHTAPP consumed $655 of $756.81 with no campaign diversity to absorb delivery gaps.
GA4 sessions spiked to 107–117 on Oct 5–6 with $0 Meta spend — sessions are decoupled from paid delivery, suggesting direct/organic traffic or GA4 data integrity issues.

suggestions.text: Diagnose and restore Meta delivery immediately; $0 spend Oct 6–7 means the account may be paused, flagged, or billing-lapsed.
suggestions.monday_update: Meta reported $0 spend and 0 leads on Oct 6 and Oct 7 — the account is either paused, payment-lapsed, or ad-flagged. Check account status, billing, and ad approvals in Meta Business Manager today. Success is confirmed when daily spend returns to the recent run rate of ~$35–$54/day. Re-check by Oct 10.

suggestions.text: Escalate all 10 overdue SOW milestones to Nacer and Sohib; Phase 1 is 69+ days behind and attribution remains blind.
suggestions.monday_update: Ten SOW milestones are overdue: the earliest (stack test, GHL migration, GBP triage, Meta CAPI, landing pages) were due 2026-07-31 and remain unconfirmed. Without these, leads cannot be traced to booked appointments, which is Phase 1's only internal benchmark. Nacer should produce a revised completion date for each item by 2026-10-12. Phase 2 conversation cannot open until at least the stack test and CAPI are verified.

suggestions.text: Watch GA4 sessions Oct 5–6 (107–117) against $0 paid spend; confirm source before attributing to organic or flagging double-count.
suggestions.monday_update: GA4 logged 107 and 117 sessions on Oct 5–6 while Meta spend was $0 both days. This decoupling is either genuine organic/direct traffic or a GA4 property misconfiguration (known risk per house rules). Pull the channel breakdown in GA4 for those two days and confirm whether sessions are direct, referral, or mis-tagged. Report back by 2026-10-11 before drawing any organic-growth conclusion.
